questions.title: Find Subarray with Given Sum (Positive Numbers)
questions.problem_statement: Given an unsorted array of non-negative integers and a target sum S, find a continuous subarray that adds up to the target sum S. Return the starting and ending 1-based indices.
questions.hint: Use a sliding window (two pointers) approach since all elements are non-negative.

questions.title: Check if Two Strings Are Anagrams
questions.problem_statement: Write a function to determine if two given strings are valid anagrams of each other (contain the exact same characters with the same frequencies).
questions.hint: Sort both character arrays or use a single frequency count array of size 26.

questions.title: Java Exception Hierarchy & Custom Exception Creation
questions.problem_statement: Explain the Throwable exception hierarchy in Java. How do you create and throw a custom user-defined exception class?
questions.hint: Extend Exception class (for checked exception) or RuntimeException class (for unchecked exception) and call super(message).

questions.title: Method Hiding vs Method Overriding in Static Methods
questions.problem_statement: Can static methods be overridden in Java? Explain Method Hiding when a subclass declares a static method with the exact signature as a static method in its superclass.
questions.hint: Static methods are bound at compile time based on reference type rather than runtime object instance.

questions.title: SQL Aggregate Functions & HAVING vs WHERE
questions.problem_statement: Differentiate between the WHERE clause and the HAVING clause in SQL. Can HAVING be used without a GROUP BY clause?
questions.hint: WHERE filters rows before grouping occurs; HAVING filters grouped aggregate results after grouping.

questions.title: DBMS Entity-Relationship (ER) Diagram & Keys
questions.problem_statement: What is an ER Diagram in DBMS? Explain Cardinality (1:1, 1:N, M:N) and Candidate Keys vs Super Keys.
questions.hint: A Super Key uniquely identifies a tuple; a Candidate Key is a minimal Super Key without redundant attributes.

questions.title: Operating Systems Paging vs Segmentation
questions.problem_statement: Compare Paging and Segmentation memory management techniques. Define Internal Fragmentation vs External Fragmentation.
questions.hint: Paging uses fixed-size memory blocks causing internal fragmentation; Segmentation uses variable-size blocks causing external fragmentation.

questions.title: Computer Networks DNS Lookup Process & IPv4 Subnetting
questions.problem_statement: Describe the step-by-step DNS Resolution process when a user types a domain URL into a browser. Differentiate Root, TLD, and Authoritative DNS servers.
questions.hint: Browser cache -> OS cache -> Recursive Resolver -> Root Server -> TLD Server -> Authoritative Nameserver.

questions.title: Probability & Marble Drawing
questions.problem_statement: A bag contains 5 red, 4 blue, and 3 green marbles. If two marbles are drawn at random without replacement, what is the probability that both are red?

questions.title: Speed, Time and Distance Boats & Streams
questions.problem_statement: A boat travels 24 km downstream in 2 hours and returns upstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.hint: Downstream speed = 24/2 = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 24/4 = 6 km/h. Still water speed = (12 + 6) / 2 = 9 km/h.

questions.title: Simple & Compound Interest Investment Growth
questions.problem_statement: An amount doubles itself in 8 years under Simple Interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.hint: Interest earned = Principal P. SI = P*R*T / 100 => P = P*R*8 / 100 => R = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.title: Logical Reasoning Syllogisms
questions.problem_statement: Statements: 'Some algorithms are fast. All fast processes are scalable.' Conclusions: I. Some algorithms are scalable. II. All scalable processes are algorithms.
questions.hint: Algorithms intersecting fast processes inherit scalability, so conclusion I is valid.

questions.title: Data Interpretation & Percentage Calculation
questions.problem_statement: A project team completed 320 tasks in Q1, which was a 25% increase over Q4 tasks. How many tasks did the team complete in Q4?

questions.title: Tell Me About Yourself
questions.problem_statement: Tell me about yourself, your educational degree, key programming skills, and core achievements.
questions.hint: Present a concise summary: educational specialization, technical competencies, major project highlight, and career goal.

questions.title: Why Do You Want to Join Infosys?
questions.problem_statement: Why do you want to join Infosys?
questions.hint: Highlight Infosys' world-class Mysore training facility, global digital services presence, strong value system (Infy values), and career growth.

questions.title: Why Should We Hire You?
questions.problem_statement: Why should Infosys hire you over other candidates?
questions.hint: Connect your solid CS foundation, problem-solving mindset, fast learning ability, and dedication with Infosys' expectations.

questions.title: Explain Your Final-Year Project
questions.problem_statement: Explain your final-year academic project. What was your specific module contribution?
questions.hint: State the problem statement, technology stack, your individual contribution, technical challenges resolved, and project impact.

questions.title: Strengths and Weaknesses
questions.problem_statement: What are your core technical strengths and an area of weakness you are working to overcome?
questions.hint: State a strong technical/analytical skill and a genuine weakness alongside the self-improvement steps you are taking.

questions.title: Describe a Challenge You Overcame
questions.problem_statement: Describe a challenging situation or technical obstacle you faced in your project and how you resolved it.
questions.hint: Follow STAR format: outline the situation, task, personal action steps taken, and successful outcome.

questions.title: Willingness to Relocate
questions.problem_statement: Are you willing to relocate to any Infosys development center across India or work in shifts?
questions.hint: Express flexibility, enthusiasm for global work culture, and commitment to project requirements.

questions.title: Five-Year Career Vision
questions.problem_statement: Where do you see yourself in five years within Infosys?
questions.hint: Express intent to master technology domain expertise, take on technical lead responsibilities, and drive key client deliverables.
